//ConnectionStrings: For running the API outside compose (dotnet run) against the composed Postgres.
Requires the dev-ports overlay, which is what publishes 5432 on the host:
docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.dev-ports.yml up postgres
Two stores, two connection strings, one database for now — the vault is a schema
inside it, reached as a role that can see nothing else.
Inside compose these are overridden by ConnectionStrings__Core and __Vault.
Dev-only credentials — see the local defaults vs. real deployment section of the README.
//Tokens: Signs access tokens. There is deliberately no built-in default anywhere in the
code, so this file is what lets `dotnet run` work outside compose. Inside compose
it is overridden by Tokens__SigningKey. Not a secret worth protecting — it is in
the repository — and not one any deployment should keep.
//Bao: For running outside compose against the composed OpenBao. Requires the dev-ports
overlay, which is what publishes 8200 on the host:
docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.dev-ports.yml up openbao-init
Inside compose these are overridden by Bao__Address and Bao__Token.
Dev-only root token — see the local defaults vs. real deployment section of the README.
//Terms: Which version of the terms signup records against the profile it creates. There is
no built-in default, so this file is what lets `dotnet run` work outside compose.
Inside compose it is overridden by Terms__CurrentVersion.
//Consent: Which version of the consent text a grant or revocation is recorded against. A
separate document from the terms above, versioned separately, so rewording either
one does not invalidate what somebody agreed to in the other. There is no built-in
default; inside compose it is overridden by Consent__PolicyVersion.
